question: What is the primary focus of a nursing audit?

options.A: Punishing nurses who make clinical errors
options.B: Evaluating the quality of nursing care and documentation

explanation: A nursing audit evaluates the quality of nursing care and documentation by comparing practice against established standards, rather than focusing on fault-finding. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which regulatory body sets the professional standards that nursing audits often measure against in Nigeria?

options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) sets the professional standards and guidelines for nursing practice and education in the country. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h1)

question: How do nursing audits contribute to professional development?

options.A: By providing free accommodation for nurses
options.B: By highlighting educational needs and areas requiring in-service training
options.C: By automatically promoting nurses to higher ranks

explanation: Audits highlight areas of weakness, showing where nursing staff may need additional in-service training or educational support. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a major role of nursing audits in quality assurance?

options.A: Measuring clinical performance against predefined criteria to ensure safety
options.B: Replacing the need for nursing supervisors
options.C: Enforcing strict punitive measures on patients
options.D: Reducing the number of nursing shifts

explanation: Audits measure clinical performance against predefined criteria to protect patient safety and promote optimal health outcomes. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: When is a retrospective nursing audit typically conducted?

options.A: While the patient is actively receiving care
options.B: Before the patient is admitted to the ward
options.C: After the patient has been discharged

explanation: Retrospective audits are performed after the patient has been discharged using completed medical records. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of a concurrent nursing audit?

options.A: It allows for immediate correction of deficiencies while the patient is still receiving care
options.B: It requires less effort than looking at discharged records
options.C: It is conducted only by the hospital director
options.D: It eliminates the need for patient consent

explanation: Concurrent audits happen in real-time, allowing nurses to immediately address and correct any identified gaps in active patient care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the first step in the nursing audit process?

options.B: Establishing specific audit criteria based on standards of care
options.C: Discharging all patients in the ward

explanation: The audit process starts by establishing clear, measurable criteria based on established standards of nursing care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is a re-audit conducted at the end of the audit cycle?

options.A: To check if implemented changes have successfully improved clinical practice
options.B: To increase the workload of student nurses
options.C: To find new staff members to discipline

explanation: A re-audit evaluates whether the corrective actions put in place have effectively resolved previous gaps and improved care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the main focus when reviewing documentation during a nursing audit?

options.A: Checking the color of the pen used by the nurse
options.B: Evaluating completeness, legibility, and accuracy of care plans and notes
options.C: Counting the total number of pages in the hospital folder
options.D: Assessing the financial cost of the documentation paper

explanation: Auditors review documentation to check for completeness, accuracy, legibility, and proper execution of the nursing process. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why must patient information be anonymized during audit data collection?

options.A: To maintain patient confidentiality and ethical standards
options.B: To make the audit report look more professional
options.C: Because patient names are unnecessary for hospital billing
options.D: To speed up the printing of audit forms

explanation: Ethical standards and confidentiality require that patient identifiers are protected during data collection for quality improvement. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the purpose of calculating compliance percentages during audit data analysis?

options.A: To determine how many nurses should be fired
options.B: To quantify performance and identify specific areas meeting or missing standards
options.C: To calculate the hospital's monthly budget
options.D: To grade nursing students on clinical placement

explanation: Compliance percentages help quantify performance and highlight exact areas where care standards are met or missed. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is root cause analysis important after identifying an audit gap?

options.A: It helps determine the underlying reason for the deficiency rather than just acknowledging it
options.B: It assigns immediate blame to the most junior nurse on duty
options.C: It removes the need to write an audit report
options.D: It automatically orders new medical equipment

explanation: Root cause analysis uncovers the true underlying causes of a problem, enabling targeted and effective solutions. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is a key requirement for successful quality improvement after an audit in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Strong leadership engagement and effective change management
options.C: Reducing the number of patients admitted
options.D: Increasing the working hours of student nurses

explanation: Strong leadership and change management are essential to effectively communicate findings and implement lasting corrective actions. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why should bedside nurses be engaged in designing solutions for identified gaps?

options.A: To ensure staff buy-in and the sustainability of the improvements
options.B: Because nurse managers are not allowed to make decisions
options.C: To reduce the salary budget of the hospital
options.D: To punish nurses who made documentation errors

explanation: Involving frontline nurses in creating solutions ensures they embrace the changes, leading to sustainable improvements in practice. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h7)

question: How does severe nursing shortage impact nursing audits in healthcare settings?

options.A: It leads to heavy workloads, rushed documentation, and increased compliance gaps
options.B: It increases the number of audits conducted daily
options.C: It eliminates the need for patient care plans
options.D: It automatically digitizes all hospital records

explanation: Staff shortages cause heavy workloads, resulting in hurried or incomplete documentation that reflects poorly during audits. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h8)

question: What cultural barrier often hinders effective nursing audits in practice?

options.A: A prevailing culture of blame rather than continuous learning
options.C: Too many trained nurse auditors in the wards
options.D: Overabundance of electronic health record systems

explanation: A culture of blame creates fear and resistance toward peer review and audits, impeding open quality improvement efforts. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h8)
